input.request: Mara wants H&V to review whether a £4.50 paper statement fee, dated 18 June 2025, was correctly applied. She says she had chosen electronic statements and disputes the fee.

events.text: A £4.50 paper statement fee dated 18 June 2025 has been applied to your account. This notification does not confirm whether the fee will be changed.

summary: Mara asked the desk to review whether a £4.50 paper statement fee dated 18 June 2025 was correctly applied, saying she had chosen electronic statements. The desk's attempt to ask the documents system about her statement preference was refused because this is a register-type request, so it registered the request with the documents team about the fee instead, and the case closed as requested. Her statement preference was not checked, the fee has not been changed or reversed, and the review itself is left to that team.

The case is cut at one moment: decide only the bank's next step from here. The facts list what the desk has read from the bank's own records so far; the conversation is what the customer and the bank said. A fact that is not listed is not known yet. The cases this desk learned from took these steps: when the customer asks something a system holds and its answer is not among the facts, the bank asks that system; when the answer is among the facts, the bank replies within it; a review, a dispute or a return goes to the team that handles it, and so does a verified customer's own instruction; anything that needs another person's authority, a secret, or a step none of the tools offers goes to a person.
